meta.description: Transition-metal d^n ions: Racah parameters, crystal-field strengths, and Tanabe-Sugano energies
references: Y. Tanabe, S. Sugano, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 9, 753 (1954) (d^n octahedral energy matrices; "On the absorption spectra of complex ions I")
Y. Tanabe, S. Sugano, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 9, 766 (1954) (part II)
A. B. P. Lever, Inorganic Electronic Spectroscopy, 2nd ed., Elsevier (1984) (standard modern source for TS matrices/formulas)
M. G. Brik, A. M. Srivastava, ECS J. Solid State Sci. Technol. 7, R3079 (2018) doi:10.1149/2.0041801jss, critical review of d3 ions (V2+, Cr3+, Mn4+, Fe5+) — cited, not re-read here (site blocked)
NIST Atomic Spectra Database (A. Kramida et al.), levels for Cr IV, Mn V, Mn III, Co III, Ni III, retrieved 2026-09-29

free_ion.note: B, C fitted here to NIST ASD 3d^n term centroids ((2J+1)-weighted) using the exact d^n Coulomb matrices in dn_ligand_field.py; fit_B_C_alpha includes Trees correction alpha*L(L+1). A plain B,C fit leaves 500-750 cm-1 rms because free-ion spectra need configuration-interaction corrections; ligand-field practice usually quotes B0 from the lowest spin-allowed separation, given as B_from_4P_minus_4F_over_15 (d3, d7) or B_from_3P_minus_3F_over_15 (d8).

commonly_quoted_textbook_B0.note: Widely quoted free-ion B values (e.g. Lever 1984 / Huheey inorganic chemistry texts); confirmed in this session only via a textbook problem statement (brainly/chegg search snippet) - treat as secondary.

host_examples.provenance_observed: Canonical ruby band maxima (~556 nm, ~410 nm) and R1 line 694.3 nm (Maiman 1960 laser line); values entered from standard knowledge, not re-fetched in this session - verify against e.g. McClure J. Chem. Phys. 36, 2757 (1962).
host_examples.derivation: Dq=E(4T2)/10; B from exact 4T1(F) formula; C from exact 2E eigenvalue of the d3 matrix (dn_ligand_field.py).

host_examples.provenance_observed: H. F. Sijbom et al., ECS J. Solid State Sci. Technol. 5, R3040 (2016) (via semanticscholar PDF, automated extraction). 4A2->4T1 band (~350-360 nm) not captured from a verified source here.
host_examples.derivation: Dq=E(4T2)/10; B,C cannot both be fixed without the 4T1 band; B shown for assumed C/B=4.5 using exact 2E eigenvalue.

gaps: Dq/B/C for Cr3+ in K2NaScF6, LiCaAlF6, GdAlO3; Mn2+ in ZnF2, KMgF3 were NOT obtained from verifiable sources in this session (publisher/PMC pages blocked).
Co2+ and Ni2+ host examples not collected.

d3_octahedral_quartets.verified: identical to exact numerical diagonalization in dn_ligand_field.py to 1e-6 cm-1

formulas.d3_doublets: Doublet block sizes (d3, octahedral; counted from exact diagonalization): 2E 4x4, 2T1 5x5, 2T2 5x5, 2A1 1x1, 2A2 1x1. No closed form for 2E/2T1/2T2 — evaluate with dn_ligand_field.DN(3).levels(B,C,Dq) (exact), or take the matrices from Tanabe & Sugano (1954) / Lever (1984) Appendix. The lowest 2E is nearly Dq-independent at large Dq/B (spin-flip within t2g^3).
formulas.d5_octahedral_exact: 4A1(G), 4E(G): E = 10B + 5C above 6A1, independent of Dq (verified numerically).

d8_octahedral.3T1g(F),3T1g(P): 7.5B + 15Dq -/+ 0.5*sqrt(225B^2 - 180B*Dq + 100Dq^2) (same form as d3 quartets, hole analogue; verified numerically)

formulas.d5_block_sizes: d5 octahedral: 6A1 1; quartets 4A1 1, 4A2 1, 4E 2, 4T1 3, 4T2 3; doublets 2A1 4, 2A2 3, 2E 7, 2T1 8, 2T2 10 (counted from exact diagonalization).
